scope: Theorem 6.3 (Cone passage) of the manuscript “Rigidity of Smooth Billiards with a Continuous Caustic Collar” (preprints/Rigidity-of-Smooth-Billiards-with-a-Continuous-Caustic-Collar-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 147 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0fefc18481d52acb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 60. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 1/2 < α < 1, a finite target aperture m0, and a fixed δb ∈ (0, H/2). There is an input aperture L, depending on α and m0, with the following property. Fix K < ∞, let d → 0, choose real centers x0, and let 0 < r ≤ Kd. Suppose rM(s) ≤ ε(d/δs)α if d/10 ≤ δs ≤ δb, |ℜs − x0| ≤ Lδs. (6.11) For sufficiently small ε > 0 and then sufficiently small d, the lift continues jointly holomorphically along vertical paths from a fixed lower row throughout d < δ < δ∗, |ℜy − x0| < m0δ, |t| < r(δ/d)α , (6.12) where δ∗ > 0 is fixed. With B = 1 + (ε/r)dα, it satisfies |s(y, t) − y| ≤ CB2 |t|2 δ1−2α . (6.13) The relative depth error is small, so these continuations remain in the shape strip, and they agree with the original lift wherever the latter is defined below them. The input aperture can be chosen independently of K. Once it contains the fixed geometric enlargements described in the proof, the constant C and the smallness requirement on ε can be chosen independently of the target aperture. They may depend on K, α, and the fixed lower-strip data.
